summary: CARICOM Heads of Government welcomed Guyana's implementation of the decision that CARICOM nationals travelling to other Member States be granted a definite entry of six months. Guyana's Foreign Ministry lists the countries whose nationals do not require visas to enter Guyana, some only for diplomatic or official passports and some for 90 or 30 days; for passport holders who require a visa and may be unable to apply at a Guyanese mission, its advisory says visas will be issued on arrival. Guyana's Immigration (Passports) Order says that, except as otherwise provided in the order, the passport of a citizen of any foreign country is not accepted unless it bears a Guyanese consular visa; it exempts passports of the countries in its schedule, passports of Commonwealth countries whose law lets Guyanese enter on their passports without a visa, passports the Minister exempts and passports covered by a Visa Abolition Agreement in force.

currencyLimits.text: Guyana's Financial Intelligence Unit says travellers carrying foreign currency amounting to more than US$10,000 or its equivalent into or out of Guyana must make a foreign currency declaration, on forms available at all international airports and border and ferry crossings, including Lethem and the Guyana/Suriname ferry. tips.text: Canada's travel advice says vehicles drive on the left, that road conditions and road safety are poor throughout the country, that roads are poorly lit and roaming livestock pose a further hazard, and advises avoiding driving at night.

Canada's travel advice says to carry enough cash to cover anticipated expenses, to exchange foreign currency only at banks, hotels and established money exchange bureaus (cambios), and that only major hotels accept credit cards. The UK government's travel advice says to go inside the money exchange or shop rather than exchange money on the street.

The UK government's travel advice says visitors can normally stay for 30 days, and that the Guyanese authorities can arrest visitors who overstay or abuse the conditions of their stay, with a possible one-year prison sentence, a fine of up to 50,000 Guyana dollars and deportation at your own expense. Immigration Support Services says it grants a maximum of two extensions of stay, each of three months. Canada's travel advice says to ensure that authorities stamp your passport on arrival.

The UK government says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk, and WHO lists Guyana itself among the countries at risk of yellow fever transmission.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guyana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. CARICOM nationals are granted a definite entry of six months. The Foreign Ministry's list of countries whose nationals do not require visas (updated 17 July 2025) names, among others, the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom, France and Italy with no period stated; Albania, Brazil and Peru for 90 days; and South Korea, Singapore and South Africa for a period not exceeding 30 days. Guatemala is listed only for holders of diplomatic or official passports and holders of a US Permanent Resident Card or a valid US, Canadian or Schengen visa. The UK government says British visitors can normally stay for 30 days. Guyana's Immigration (Passports) Order says that, except as otherwise provided in the order, the passport of a citizen of any foreign country is not accepted unless it bears a Guyanese consular visa; it exempts passports of the countries in its schedule, passports of Commonwealth countries whose law lets Guyanese enter on their passports without a visa, passports the Minister exempts and passports covered by a Visa Abolition Agreement in force.

faq.question: How does CARICOM free movement work in Guyana?
faq.answer: CARICOM Heads of Government welcomed Guyana's implementation of the decision that CARICOM nationals travelling to other Member States be granted a definite entry of six months, subject to the right of Member States to reject undesirable persons and to prevent persons from becoming a charge on public funds.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Guyana?
faq.answer: WHO lists Guyana as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries at risk of yellow fever transmission, including travellers who transited more than 4 hours through the airport of such a country, and lists Guyana itself as a country at risk of yellow fever transmission.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Guyana?
faq.answer: The Foreign Ministry's advisory says that for persons travelling from countries whose passport holders require a visa to enter Guyana and who may be unable to apply at any of Guyana's missions or consulates, visas will be issued on arrival. Immigration Support Services takes the visitor visa application online, with a mandatory letter requesting a visa on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Guyana?
faq.answer: Yes. Immigration Support Services takes extension applications with a letter to its Head requesting the extension and evidence of finance to cover the extended stay. It says each extension is for three months, that a maximum of two are granted, and that the processing fee is GYD 5,125 (GYD 28,700 if the extension granted exceeds three months).

faq.question: Is Guyana safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says attacks and muggings, sometimes with knives or firearms, have occurred in broad daylight but are more common at night, names Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and Sophia in Georgetown among the areas affected, and suggests arranging a car or taxi booked by your hotel or with a licensed operator. Canada's travel advice says travel to the interior is not safe due to low police presence, and the UK says medical facilities are very limited, even in Georgetown.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: There are two rainy seasons in Guyana: from May to July and from November to January. However, flooding occurs year round and can hamper overland travel and reduce the provision of essential services, particularly in coastal areas.

entryRequirements.overstay.text: 13. If an immigrant to whom a permit has been granted under section 12 fails to leave Guyana on or before the expiration of the period for which the permit has been granted, he shall, unless such period has been extended as provided in subsection (3) of that section, be deemed to be a prohibited immigrant.

(1A) The immigration officer shall specify in the permit, granted under subsection (1) that the immigrant is granted the permit – (a) as a passenger in transit; or (b) for medical treatment; or (c) as a visitor; or (d) for purposes of employment; or (e) for purposes of trade or business; or (f) for any other purpose of a temporary nature.

16. (l) An immigration officer who decides that an immigrant is a prohibited immigrant may in his discretion— (a) order him to leave Guyana and proceed immediately by the same vessel (or other means of transportation) by which he arrived; (b) order him to leave Guyana within a specified period to be determined by the immigration officer; or (c) cause him to be arrested and brought before a magistrate’s court, with a view to an order being made for his removal from Guyana.

levies.travel-tax.text: All travelers under the age of sixty-five (65), unless exempted, must pay the full Travel Tax of Three thousand five hundred dollars ($3,500).
Travel tax is now incorporated into your travel itinerary and you are no longer required to make this payment at the airport.
Eligible persons must be in possession of a valid Guyanese passport and have been residing in Guyana for a period no less than 183 days in a given year.

levies.name: Travel Tax
levies.text: The Guyana Revenue Authority says all travellers under 65, unless exempted, pay a Travel Tax of GYD 3,500, which is now included in the travel itinerary instead of being paid at the airport. The reduced rate for people aged 65 or over requires a Guyanese passport and residence in Guyana.
